newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hamas rejects Israeli-Palestinian deal on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Hamas rejects Israeli-Palestinian deal on Hebron.

text.p: The militant Islamic group Hamas said on Wednesday it rejected a Palestinian-Israeli deal extending Palestinian rule to the West Bank town of Hebron and warned self-rule authorities against cracking down on militants.
"Hamas rejects this pact which is an extension to the Oslo accord," the group, which opposes the 1993 Palestinian-Israeli peace agreement, said in a statement.
Under the pact concluded early on Wednesday Israel will hand over most of Hebron to Palestinian rule within 10 days.
In its statement, Hamas warned the Palestinian self-rule authorities against pursuing militants under what it said were pledges made by President Yasser Arafat as part of the deal.

Hamas "warns the Palestinian authority against launching an arrest campaign against the movement...especially in the area of Hebron and against hitting the group's infrastructure in accordance with pledges made under the deal," it said.

Last year Palestinian authorities launched a widescale arrest campaign against militants in the West Bank self-ruled territories after Hamas carried out suicide bombing attacks in Israel in February and March.
Details of the Hebron accord, which negotiators initialled on the border between Israel and the Gaza Strip, have not been made public.
"This submissive settlement will ease political pressures on (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu and will attempt to portray him internationally as a man of peace," Hamas said.

"Hamas is committed to its political programme and holy struggle in the face of the Zionist and (Palestinian) authority's campaign which targets this strategic Palestinian agenda. Victory in the end will be for truth and justice and defeat for tyranny and occupation," the group added.
